subject.title: chatCompletions: ignore request model when x-openclaw-agent-id header is present

question: Should a valid `x-openclaw-agent-id` make OpenAI-compatible requests tolerate or ignore a generic body `model`, despite the current documented agent-first model contract?
rationale: The code path is narrow, but the behavior changes a public Gateway API contract and affects parity across Chat Completions, Responses, and embeddings.

options.title: Adopt Header Precedence
options.body: Treat a generic body `model` as client compatibility metadata whenever a valid agent header selects the agent, and update shared resolver behavior plus docs/tests for the selected endpoints.

options.title: Preserve Agent-First Contract
options.body: Continue requiring the body `model` to be `openclaw`, `openclaw/default`, or `openclaw/<agentId>`, and document SDK integrations around those values plus optional `x-openclaw-model`.

options.title: Decide Shared Endpoint Semantics First
options.body: Keep this open until Gateway owners choose one consistent precedence rule for Chat Completions, Responses, and embeddings before implementation.

recommendation.title: Decide Shared Endpoint Semantics First
recommendation.body: Keep this open until Gateway owners choose one consistent precedence rule for Chat Completions, Responses, and embeddings before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: The agent-first OpenAI-compatible model contract and related endpoint expansion trace to vincentkoc's commits and merged PR history.
